limitations: SIGKILL can prevent terminal receipts; cold=RUNNING after process death is stale, not a successful or still-active run.
Stage spans are first-to-last inner samples; do not attribute the entire host deadline to claims.
Independent memory component peaks occur at different times and must not be summed.
RSS sums can double-count shared pages; kernel charge is the authoritative process-tree limit.
A last sampled counter may precede a subsequent Docker-confirmed OOM kill.
Committed aggregate profiles may precede death; they are not terminal or complete-output receipts.
CPU/IO/pressure totals cover the whole experiment, not a single operation; counters do not identify Python objects or individual spill/DB/blob files.
Database integrity after exit is not fresh-worker recovery; neither revision published complete output.

preserved_memory.scope: Only application inner/host samples; deliberate OOM probe samples excluded
